contexts.text: (Abraham) bowed himself towards the earth () = the effect of humiliation from joy thence. To bow = to humble. See AC 4347.
(Lot) bowed himself the face to the earth () = humiliation. Explained.
Abraham arose and bowed himself () = the Lord's joy on account of a kind reception... To bow himself = to rejoice. Bowing is a gesture of both humiliation and joy. AC 2950. AC 3163.
Under Bend, see this reference, and at AC 5682. AC 7068.
Peoples shall bow themselves to Thee () = truths of good.
(Jacob) bowed himself to the earth seven times () = submission of all things. AC 4360. AC 4361. AC 4362. AC 6366.
They bowed themselves to my sheaf () = adoration. To bow one's self = the effect of humiliation, thus adoration. AC 4698. AC 4701.
They bowed down, etc. () treats of those who are being instructed in truths and led to good.
They bowed themselves to him the face to the earth () = humiliation. To bow one's self = humiliation; and the face to the earth = the humiliation of adoration. Explained. AC 5676. AC 6266. AC 7788.
Israel bowed himself upon the head of the bed () = that he turned himself to those things which are of the interior natural. To bow himself, here = to turn himself.
Bowing is such an act of the body as corresponds to the humiliation of the mind; hence they who are in the adoration of God from the heart thus bow themselves.
He stooped down, etc. () = to put himself in power; for when a lion stoops down he hardens his nerves, and makes himself strong. AR 241:2. AE 278:3.
(Moses) bowed himself () = admission; because predicated of truth Divine.
Thou shalt not bow thyself to their gods () = that the falsities of evil are not to be worshipped. To bow one's self = adoration and worship. AC 10553. AC 10645. AE 410:3.
Ye shall bow yourselves afar off () = humiliation and adoration from the heart, and then the Lord's influx. Explained.
Humiliation before man produces bowing according to the estimation in which he is held, but before the Divine a complete bowing down. Explained.
